{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "martinus",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "reviewed code, reported a rebase compile error, warned against Result<bool>, and suggested multiple template and test improvements"
    },
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "asked how types convertible to bool and Result<optional<T>> are handled"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "suggested keeping PR in draft while CI is red and based on other PRs"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:1167821634",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "use a bool template argument instead of passing a lambda to simplify recursive Construct calls",
      "quote": "It took me a while to figure out what's going on here with the recursive `Construct` calls and the lambda that's passed along. How about instead of passing a lambda along use a `bool` template argument",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author adopted the suggestion renaming the template argument to Failure and pushed the change",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1182977847"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1182977847",
      "status_by_quote": "Thanks, that's much better! Took suggestion jsut renaming argument to \"Failure\""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1167981120",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "explicitly mark move-assignment operator as deleted for clearer compiler error messages",
      "quote": "Mayby explicitly mark the move-assignment as delete",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author marked the operator deleted and added a comment",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1182978622"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1182978622",
      "status_by_quote": "Thanks, that changes error message from `error: object of type 'util::Result<int>' cannot be assigned because its copy assignment operator is implicitly deleted` to `error: overload resolution selected deleted operator=`"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1167981676",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "remove unnecessary check if (!src.m_info->errors.empty())",
      "quote": "nit: I don't think the `if (!src.m_info->errors.empty())` check is necessary.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained the check avoids allocating ErrorInfo in the common error-free case",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1182978708"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1182978708",
      "status_by_quote": "It's not strictly necessary, but it avoids allocating an ErrorInfo object in the common case where there are no errors or warnings."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:1518662504",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "compile error in spend.cpp ChooseSelectionResult after rebase",
      "quote": "After rebasing I get a compile error in `spend.cpp`  `ChooseSelectionResult`, adding a bunch of `std::move` helps",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "fixed in rebase",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "r:1409772815",
      "status_by_quote": "making most of the suggested changes"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1174297928",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "allowing Result<bool> is error-prone because Result converts to bool for success or failure",
      "quote": "maybe consider forbidding type `bool` for `T`. I recently had similar code in another project, and its utterly confusing; because Result can convert to bool but that only tells if it *has* a bool or not. It's very error prone.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed that types like bool and optional<T> are ambiguous and should be disallowed, while clarifying pointers and ints should remain allowed",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1269813522"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1269813522",
      "status_by_quote": "I agree with all of this and want to do more work to address it."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1174298529",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "add static_assert checks to ensure sizeof(util::Result) matches expected size",
      "quote": "I'd add a check somewhere to ensure that the size of the Result is as claimed in the commit message",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added static_asserts in result_tests.cpp",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1182977109"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1182977109",
      "status_by_quote": "Thanks, added to result_tests.cpp"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1174414223",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "mark move constructors noexcept along with methods they use",
      "quote": "move constructors should usually be `noexcept`, but then all methods it uses also have to be `noexcept`.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained conditions required for noexcept and deferred optimization for later",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1182978551"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1182978551",
      "status_by_quote": "Right now I'm just trying to do the simplest thing that's correct, and I think probably in most cases where the result class is used, having the move constructor be marked noexcept isn't going impact performance."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1233967699",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "how are Result<std::optional<T>> and other types implementing operator bool() handled",
      "quote": "I guess the same goes for something like `Result<std::optional<int>, int>`, or really any type implementing `operator bool()`? How did you handle these cases in your code?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author answered agreeing that Result<optional<T>> is ambiguous and should be disallowed",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:1269813522"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:1269813522",
      "status_by_quote": "I think by default types convertible to bool should be disallowed with `Result`. I think `Result<bool>` or `Result<optional<T>>` types are inherently ambiguous"
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:1386736519",
      "verdict": "",
      "reason": "This makes util::Result quite a bit more powerful, and it's still simple to use.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "src/util/result.h"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "author is keeping PR in draft while updating commits and waiting on base PRs #25665 and #26022",
      "id": "c:1960225482"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Re-read converted schema 1 items: reclassified rc:1167821634 to suggestion, and updated status of rc:1174297928 to answered rather than fixed. Added suggestions from martinus and question from sedited."
}
